Heritage Oaks Hospital is seeking a talented and dynamic Outpatient Clinical Manager to lead a team of dedicated healthcare professionals!

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Outpatient Clinical Program Manager provides administrative leadership and clinical supervision to the Outpatient Services Department, ensuring appropriate psychosocial treatment programs that meet the needs of the patients and the community and are in compliance with regulatory agencies and the facility’s performance objectives. Responsibilities include managing the administrative, and clinical processes for all Outpatient Services offered at the facility. The Clinical Manager position is a dynamic role that provides administrative leadership and clinical oversight to a growing multi-disciplinary team of RNs, Master’s level Therapists, Case Managers, and Licensed Therapists. Outpatient offers a myriad of programs including Partial Hospitalization, Dual Diagnosis PHP, Intensive Outpatient (IOP), Chemical Dependency Intensive Outpatient, Adolescent PHP, and Adolescent IOP.

The ideal candidate will have a broad experience in the psychiatric/mental health field, with a minimum of two (2) years’ experience in advanced clinical/management practice preferred. You must have Master’s Degree in Counseling, Psychology or Social Work and hold a LCSW.

Education:
Graduate of an accredited school of social work or related field and licensed by the California Board of Behavioral Sciences.

Experience:
Minimum of five (5) years’ experience in psychiatric/mental health field, with a minimum of two (2) years’ experience in advanced clinical/management practice preferred.

License:
California Licensed Clinical Social Worker, Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, or Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor and a valid driver’s license.

Additional Requirements:
A strong knowledge of JCAHO, NAPHS, Title XXII, CMS, OSHA regulations, and patient rights standards and all other applicable federal and state laws and regulations governing mental health care facilities. CPR certification, and successful completion of the hospital’s designated behavioral and physical management training program, including de-escalation and appropriate use of seclusion and restraint required prior to assisting in the procedures.

jobs.title: PSH PBV Case Manager
jobs.description:
Location:
Gardena, California

Salary:
$25.48 per hour

Organization Overview

Founded in 2004, Brilliant Corners provides innovative housing and housing-related services to California's most vulnerable individuals, with an emphasis on those transitioning from, or at risk of, homelessness or institutionalization. We develop, own, and manage multi-family supportive housing and licensed residential care homes. We implement a broad array of scattered-site, one-on-one supportive housing, and clinical case management programs through partnerships with developmental services, homeless services, veterans' services, and health care sectors.

In short, we do good work.

We have offices statewide with a staff of passionate people. While we are growing rapidly, we are also selective: We're seeking inspired, talented people who want to effect profound change and who have fun doing it.

Program Summary

The Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH)-Project Based program is supported by Los Angeles County Homeless Services & Housing (HSH) and serves individuals experiencing homelessness who have a chronic illness or physical disability. The goal is to transition individuals out of homelessness and into permanent housing, in order to obtain stability in all areas of their lives. Services take place within residential communities for individuals who are experiencing homelessness and eligible for PSH at a project site.

Position Summary

The Case Manager, Permanent Supportive Housing Project Based (PSH-PB) will provide intensive case management services to a caseload of up to 20 homeless individuals who are eligible for permanent supportive housing at the project site located in the Gardena, CA area. The Case Manager will assist clients to achieve and maintain health, mental health, and housing stability. The Case Manager plays a critical role in supporting clients to thrive in their new homes through a client-centered and "whatever it takes" approach to services.

Responsibilities

Accept, screen, and process referrals from HSH and other HSH partners
Conduct outreach and engagement in the community in order to locate referrals once they have been assigned by HSH
Conduct assessments and re-assessments, including a comprehensive psychosocial assessment, in order to determine clients' eligibility for the program and evaluate clients' needs and strengths
Develop and implement individualized case management services plans that ensure housing stability and identify short and long-term goals
Provide support throughout the housing process including but not limited to temporary housing placement, unit identification, application submissions, lease-up coordination, and ongoing housing retention
Provide education to clients on tenant rights and responsibilities, eviction prevention counseling and advocacy
Provide linkage to community resources, benefits, and services which may include physical and mental health, substance use treatment, education/vocational programs, employment services, health insurance, disability benefits, and other sources of financial assistance
Meet with clients frequently and regularly in the home on project site, community, and office and accompany clients to appointments as needed
Provide crisis intervention and ensure that clients have access to the 24/7 case management crisis line
Provide life skills education and assistance, including budgeting, apartment upkeep, stress management, conflict resolution, etc
Provide transportation assistance, including transportation via personal vehicle
Participate in case conferences to review clients' progress and address any challenges, with particular emphasis on case coordination and conferencing with onsite property management to discuss housing related challenges and concerns
Collaborate and communicate with HSH partners on a regular basis
Build and maintain partnerships with community organizations, service providers, public entities, and onsite property management to ensure that clients have access to comprehensive services
Maintain updated and accurate client files and documentation
Participate in staff meetings and other agency events as requested

Requirements

Professional Experience

At least 1 year of experience working with homeless individuals and a Bachelor's Degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology or a related field OR at least 2 years of experience providing direct mental health and/or intensive case management services
Experience working with individuals who have a mental illness, chronic health issue, and/or substance use disorder
Experience working at a project based site preferred

Knowledge Skills And Ability

Strong interpersonal and client engagement skills
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Flexibility regarding scheduling and prioritizing of tasks
Willingness to travel and spend significant time in the field
Able to transport clients in your vehicle
Basic computer knowledge (MS Word and Excel required)
Familiarity with evidence-based interventions including Harm Reduction, Trauma Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing
Ability to work independently and utilize critical thinking skills in decision-making situations
Good organizational and record-keeping skills
Possession of a valid, clean California driver's license and a personal insured vehicle are required
Bilingual in English/Spanish preferred

Core Competencies

Interpersonal Savvy: Builds trusting relationships, skillfully engages others, and collaborates effectively to drive success
Conflict Management: Addresses conflicts by understanding needs, employing empathetic listening, identifying underlying issues and facilitating equitable solutions that respect all parties
Dealing with Paradox: Flexibly adjusts approaches to meet complex needs; balances conflicting demands with adaptability and rapport while maintaining boundaries

Organizational Values

Humanity: Putting people first: We are committed to meeting people where they're at, honoring their dignity, diversity, and experience
Community: Building a better future: Sustainable housing solutions are fostered through partnership, collaboration, and human connection
Ingenuity: Innovating for transformation: Systems-change requires relentless determination, thinking outside the box and challenging the status quo

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations

A valid, clean CA driver's license and a personal insured vehicle are required.

Labor Union

This position is part of the OPEIU, LOCAL 30, AFL-CIO, bargaining unit. As a member of the OPEIU, LOCAL 30, AFL-CIO, the incumbent will be subject to the terms and conditions outlined in the collective bargaining agreement.

Physical Requirements

Candidates should have physical mobility for tasks such as standing, bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, twisting, and walking on uneven surfaces. They should be capable of performing stationary tasks like sitting for up to 6 to 8 hours a day. Additionally, candidates should be able to lift, carry, push, pull light to moderate weights up to 15 pounds safely. Requires mental acuity for analytical reasoning and document interpretation.

The salary range for this position is $25.48 - $26.50. This position is being offered at $25.48 per hour.

These activities include, but are not limited to, hiring and firing of staff, selection of volunteers and vendors, and provision of services. We are committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all members of our staff, clients, volunteers, subcontractors, vendors, and clients. W e will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Benefits

Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental, & Vision)
Retirement Plan (With 5% Match)
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary and AD&D)
Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
Short Term & Long-Term Disability
Training & Development

Medical Case Manager (LVN) (PACE - Utilization Management)

CalOptima

Join Us in this Amazing Opportunity

The Team You'll Join

We are a mission driven community-based organization that serves member health with excellence and dignity, respecting the value and needs of each person. If you are ready to advance your career while making a difference, we encourage you to review and apply today and help us build healthier communities for all.

More About The Opportunity

We are hoping you will join us as a Medical Case Manager (LVN) (PACE-Utilization Management)
and help shape the future of healthcare where you'll be an integral part of our PACE- Clinic
team, helping to strive for excellence while we serve our member health with dignity, respecting the value and needs of each of our members through collaboration with our providers, community partners and local stakeholders. This position has been approved to be Partial Telework
.

If telework is approved, you are required to work within the State of California only and if Partial Telework, also come in to the Main Office in Orange, CA, at least two (2) days per week minimum.

The Medical Case Manager (LVN) for the Program for All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) is responsible for reviewing and processing requests for authorization and notification of medical services from health professionals, clinical facilities, and ancillary providers. You will be responsible for prior authorization, concurrent review and referral related processes which include on-line responsibilities as well as selected off-line tasks. You utilizes PACE medical criteria, policies, and procedures to authorize referral requests from medical professionals, clinical facilities, and ancillary providers. You directly interacts with provider callers and serves as a resource for their needs. Together, we are building a stronger, more equitable health system.

Your Contributions To The Team

95% - Case Management
Participates in a mission-driven culture of high-quality performance, with a member focus on customer service, consistency, dignity and accountability.
Assists the team in carrying out department responsibilities and collaborates with others to support short- and long-term goals/priorities for the department.
Reviews requests for medical appropriateness for inpatient and outpatient services utilizing medical criteria and/or established policies and procedures.
Verifies and processes specialty referrals, diagnostic testing, outpatient procedures, home health care services and durable medical equipment and supplies via telephone or fax by using established clinical protocols to determine medical necessity.
Screens inpatient and outpatient requests for the PACE Medical Director review, gathers pertinent medical information prior to submission to the PACE Medical Director; follows up with the requester by communicating the PACE Medical Director's decision; documents follow-up in the utilization management system.
Completes required documentation for data entry into the utilization management system at the time of receipt to include any authorization updates.
Reviews ICD-10, CPT-4, and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes for accuracy and existence of coverage specific to the PACE.
Ensures all internal and external PACE authorizations are complete with CPT codes, notes and pertinent information.
Reviews the appropriateness of retro authorizations for review and works with the PACE Medical Director for proper review and authorizations.
Reviews and follows up on denied claims and provider disputes/appeals to ensure accuracy of information and maintain partnerships with our contracted specialty offices.
Refers cases of possible over/under utilization to the PACE Medical Director for proper reporting and reviewing.
Meets PACE productivity and quality of work standards on an ongoing basis.
Assists the manager with identifying areas of need for staff training and maintains current data resources.

5% - Other
Completes other projects and duties as assigned.

Do You Have What the Role Requires?

High school diploma or equivalent PLUS 3 years of nursing experience, with 1 year as a nurse reviewer, required; an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the position such as those listed above may also be qualifying.
CPR and First-Aid Certification required or must be obtained within six (6) months of date of hire.

You'll Stand Out More If You Possess The Following

Managed care experience.
Concurrent review experience.

What the Regulatory Agencies Need You to Possess?

Current unrestricted Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) license to practice in the state of California.

Your Knowledge & Abilities To Bring To This Role

Develop rapport and establish and maintain effective working relationships with CalOptima Health's leadership and staff and external contacts at all levels and with diverse backgrounds.
Work independently and exercise sound judgment.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
Work a flexible schedule; available to participate in evening and weekend events.
Organize, be analytical, problem-solve and possess project management skills.
Work in a fast-paced environment and in an efficient manner.
Manage multiple projects and identify opportunities for internal and external collaboration.
Motivate and lead multi-program teams and external committees/coalitions.
Utilize computer and appropriate software (e.g., Microsoft Office: Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and job specific applications/systems to produce correspondence, charts, spreadsheets, and/or other information applicable to the position assignment.

Your Physical Requirements (With Or Without Accommodations)

Ability to visually read information from computer screens, forms and other printed materials and information.
Ability to speak (enunciate) clearly in conversation and general communication.
Hearing ability for verbal communication/conversation/responses via telephone, telephone systems, and face-to-face interactions.
Manual dexterity for typing, writing, standing and reaching, flexibility, body movement for bending, crouching, walking, kneeling and prolonged sitting.
Lifting and moving objects, patients and/or equipment 10 to 25 pounds

jobs.description:
Summary

This Pharmacist (Facility Program Manager) functions as a Medication Safety Officer for the Pharmacy Service. This important leadership position will work collaboratively with Pharmacy - Nursing - and health care system leadership and staff. The incumbent manages/coordinates all medication safety - performance improvement - and regulatory (e.g. - VHA - DEA - Joint Commission - USP - EPA - etc.) compliance for the service.

Qualifications

Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Basic Requirements

United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy
English Language Proficiency: Pharmacists must be proficient in spoken and written English as required by 38 U.S.C. 7402(d) - and 7407(d)
Education: Graduate of an Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredited College or School of Pharmacy with a baccalaureate degree in pharmacy (BS Pharmacy) and/or a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D. degree
(NOTE: Prior to 2005 ACPE accredited both baccalaureate and Doctor of Pharmacy terminal degree program
Today the sole degree is Doctor of Pharmacy)
TRANSCRIPTS MUST BE SUBMITTED WITH APPLICATION OR Graduates of foreign pharmacy degree programs meet the educational requirement if the graduate is able to provide proof of achieving the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Commission (FPGEC) Certification - which includes passing the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Equivalency Examination (FPGEE) and the Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT)
YOU MUST SUBMIT COPY OF FPGEC CERTIFICATION WITH THE APPLICATION PACKAGE
Licensure
Full - current and unrestricted license to practice pharmacy in a State - Territory - Commonwealth of the United States (i.e. - Puerto Rico) - or the District of Columbia
The pharmacist must maintain current registration if this is a requirement for maintaining full - current - and unrestricted licensure
A pharmacist who has - or has ever had - any license(s) revoked - suspended - denied - restricted - limited - or issued/placed in a probationary status may be appointed only in accordance with the provisions in VA Handbook 5005 - Part II - Chapter 3 - section B - paragraph 16
YOU MUST SUBMIT A COPY OF CURRENT LICENSE WITH THE APPLICATION PACKAGE
Creditable Experience Knowledge of Professional Pharmacy Practices
To be creditable - the experience must have demonstrated the use of knowledge - skills - and abilities associated with professional pharmacy practice
Professional practice means paid/non-paid employment as a professional or unlicensed graduate pharmacist as defined by the appropriate licensing board
Quality of Experience
Qualifying experience must be at a level comparable to pharmacy experience at the next lower level
Experience as a Graduate Pharmacist is creditable provided the candidate was used as a professional pharmacist (under supervision) and subsequently passed the appropriate licensure examination
Part-time Experience
Part-time experience as a professional pharmacist is credited according to its relationship to the full-time workweek

Program Manager - Individual and Family Plans, Covered California

CalOptima

Join Us in this Amazing Opportunity

The Team You'll Join

We are a mission driven community-based organization that serves member health with excellence and dignity, respecting the value and needs of each person. If you are ready to advance your career while making a difference, we encourage you to review and apply today and help us build healthier communities for all.

More About The Opportunity

We are hoping you will join us as a Program Manager - Individual and Family Plans, Covered California
and help shape the future of healthcare where you'll be an integral part of our Strategic Development
team, helping to strive for excellence while we serve our member health with dignity, respecting the value and needs of each of our members through collaboration with our providers, community partners and local stakeholders. This position has been approved to be Partial Telework
.

If telework is approved, you are required to work within the State of California only and if Partial Telework, also come in to the Main Office in Orange, CA, at least two (2) days per week minimum.

The Program Manager plays a vital role in supporting the design, development, and implementation of Strategic Development programs and new product lines, including commercial. You will be responsible for coordination, implementation, execution and completion of tasks supporting new program development and implementation. You will assist in the overall day-to-day activities, cross-functional projects and department assignments related to program development, operations, and project coordination. You will regularly collaborate with CalOptima Health's staff across departments to support related projects and may interact with executives, management, and legal counsel. Together, we are building a stronger, more equitable health system.

Your Contributions To The Team

85% - Program Support
Participates in a mission-driven culture of high-quality performance, with a member focus on customer service, consistency, dignity and accountability.
Provides program recommendations, guidance, risk management and support of end-to-end operations and interdependencies.
Ensures strategic direction of projects/program is in line with department goals and CalOptima Health's strategic priorities.
Makes moderate to significant improvements of processes, systems or products to enhance performance of job area.
Plans and implements multiple projects/programs spanning across business areas.
Tracks and reports on health care marketplace conditions, marketplace requirements and policy developments/changes to support senior level staff.
Supports the review and analysis of information from different sources focused on health care initiatives, new programs or focus areas as assigned.
Supports subject matter experts to review data sources, evaluate new initiatives, develop summary reports, formulate conclusions and make recommendations for leadership consideration.
Tracks and manages concurrent initiatives ensuring all projects meet success parameters and targets.
Drafts workplans for assigned projects and assignments, and manages the scope, schedule, budget and quality of the project.
Drafts workflows, key performance indicator (KPI) dashboards, procedures and/or policies and recommends changes to ensure timely, efficient and effective outputs.
Drafts presentations, board reports and memos to support senior management.
Prepares routine reports and summaries for internal departments, external stakeholders and state agencies.
Supports project workgroup activities.

10% - Administrative Support
Assists, shares knowledge with and mentors CalOptima Health staff regarding standards, organizational understanding and relationship building to promote successful delivery of projects.
Assists the team in carrying out department responsibilities and collaborates with others to support short- and long-term goals/priorities for the department.
Assists management with vendor support and purchasing activities related to strategic programs and pilots for the department.
Supports the day-to-day Covered California team administrative activities.

5% - Completes other projects and duties as assigned.

Do You Have What the Role Requires?

Bachelor's degree in public health, business, health care administration or related field PLUS 3 years of experience in health care programs, including cross-collaboration and coordination, and internal and external stakeholder engagement (e.g. member/patient, provider, community, health networks, contractor/vendor etc.) required; an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the position such as those listed above may also be qualifying.
Experience at a health plan, health system, health provider, public agency or hospital setting required.

Master's degree.

Managed care operations experience.
2 years of experience and aptitude for working in a highly matrixed, mission-driven organization.

n/a

Develop rapport and establish and maintain effective working relationships with CalOptima Health's leadership and staff and external contacts at all levels and with diverse backgrounds.
Work independently and exercise sound judgment.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
Work a flexible schedule; available to participate in evening and weekend events.
Organize, be analytical, problem-solve and possess project management skills.
Work in a fast-paced environment and in an efficient manner.
Manage multiple projects and identify opportunities for internal and external collaboration.
Motivate and lead multi-program teams and external committees/coalitions.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Vendor and Scaled Operations
jobs.description:
Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.

Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.

About The Service Operations Team

We're a tight-knit team of program management, process & automation, and workforce management professionals working together to deliver world-class service through operational excellence and strategic enablement. We collaborate closely with frontline Service, Business Apps, QA, Enablement, and Analytics teams to plan and deliver on complex initiatives that improve processes, tools, and how our service operates day-to-day. Our focus is on creating service experiences that are both efficient for our operations team while providing an excellent experience for our customers and pros.

About The Role

As a Senior Program Manager, Vendor & Scaled Operations within Thumbtack's Service Operations PMO, you will own our outsourced and scaled delivery model - the strategy, the governance, and the long-horizon programs that determine how a meaningful share of our service gets delivered. This is not a generalist PM role. It is purpose-built for someone who can hold a commercial relationship, an operational system, and an executive narrative at the same time.

You will own Thumbtack's vendor and BPO strategy for Service Operations end to end: how we decide what to outsource, how we hold partners accountable, how we govern performance, and how we scale or unwind capacity as the business changes. You'll own a portfolio of scaled operations and partner support programs spanning a year or more, with real interdependencies between them, and you'll make the prioritization and capacity calls across that portfolio rather than escalating them.

You'll also be the person leadership turns to for the make-versus-buy conversation. Expect to build the cost, quality, and risk case for how we scale, bring it to senior leaders and to vendor executives, and then be accountable for the model you recommended.

This is a high-leverage, high-ambiguity role. Much of the infrastructure you'll need does not fully exist yet, and building it durably - so it outlasts you - is a core part of the job.

What You’ll Do

Own Thumbtack's vendor and outsourcing strategy for Service Operations - sourcing decisions, make-versus-buy recommendations, capacity strategy across internal, vendor, and partner channels, and the case for expanding, consolidating, or exiting a partner. Own the commercial relationship alongside Legal, Finance, and Procurement (SOWs, rate structures, SLA credits and remedies, renewals) and know which levers to pull when performance slips.
Design and optimize the governance model for vendor performance: SLA and scorecard architecture, QBR structure, decision rights, escalation paths, and remediation playbooks. Build durable frameworks, not one-off trackers.
Own a portfolio of programs. Set the strategy, sequence the work, decide what does and doesn't get done, drive it to business-level outcomes, and establish the operating rhythms - cadences, decision logs, dependency tracking, escalation thresholds, change communication - that keep distributed, multi-party delivery predictable.
Build the measurement framework for the scaled delivery model: quality, SLA attainment, forecast accuracy, cost-to-serve, and the leading indicators that reveal a program is silently degrading before the lagging metrics do. Define what "good" looks like and close the loop so performance data actually changes behavior - on our side and the vendor's.
Align senior leaders and lead the change. Bring executives across Service Operations, IT, Legal, Finance, Product, and Workforce Management to a decision on sourcing priorities and tradeoffs, translating tangled multi-party problems into a clear recommendation - then drive adoption through teams and partners who don't report to you, including the unglamorous follow-through that determines whether change sticks.
Raise the bar on how this work gets done. Identify and build AI and automation that reduces coordination overhead and improves oversight at scale, and coach other program managers while institutionalizing what works into playbooks and standards, so every future partnership starts from a higher floor.

In order to be successful, you must bring

8+ years in program or project management, including 3+ years owning vendor, BPO, or outsourced delivery relationships at scale. Experience with multiple vendors, multiple sites, or a vendor transition is strongly preferred. Proficiency in program management tooling (e.g., Jira, Linear, Coda, Smartsheet) and fluency across Agile and Waterfall approaches. PMP, PgMP, or equivalent is nice-to-have.
Deep vendor ownership and sourcing judgment. You've personally owned an outsourcing relationship end to end - commercial terms, governance, performance management, escalation, and the hard conversations - not just coordinated with one someone else owned. You've also built and defended a make-versus-buy or vendor expansion case with cost, quality, and risk modeling, and taken it to senior leadership.
Portfolio-level ownership. You've run multiple concurrent scale programs with genuine tradeoffs between them, and owned the prioritization and capacity calls yourself. You've run programs where consistency of human execution at volume is the product - you know how to design for repeatability, and you spot degradation from leading indicators rather than after the fact.
A track record of building durable infrastructure. SLA and scorecard architecture, governance models, transition playbooks, reporting systems - things other teams adopted and still use. You build and maintain the models, dashboards, and SLA tracking yourself rather than waiting for someone else to instrument it.
Comfort where the playbook doesn't exist, and a habit of leaving people better than you found them. You've stepped into situations with no established approach and built one, with the judgment to know when structure helps and when it would slow things down - and you've mentored program managers or been the person other teams borrow practices from.

Expected salary ranges

For candidates living in San Francisco / Bay Area, San Jose, New York City, or Seattle metros, the expected total cash compensation (base salary + variable pay, if applicable) range for the role is currently $153,000 - $198,000
For candidates living in Austin, TX or Washington DC metros or in California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, or Washington states, the expected total cash compensation (base salary + variable pay, if applicable) range for the role is currently $137,700 - $178,200
For candidates living in all other US locations, the expected total cash compensation (base salary + variable pay, if applicable) range for this role is currently $130,100- $168,300

Actual offered salaries will vary and will be based on various factors, such as calibrated job level, qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.

jobs.title: Housing Case Manager Shelter Plus Care Berkeley Respite
jobs.description:
Company Overview

For more than 50 years, Insight Housing has provided a comprehensive range of housing, food, and support services to help those in need move from homelessness into a safe and affordable home of their own. We serve in seven counties in the bay area - Alameda, San Francisco, Contra Costa, Solano, Sacramento, San Joaquin, and Amador County. We are proud of our team members who are very dedicated to our mission of ensuring everyone in our community has a home through supportive, equitable, and sustainable housing solutions.

Program Overview

Shelter Plus Care
(S+C): Funded by the City of Berkeley, the Shelter Plus Care program provides permanent supportive housing to adults who are chronically homeless and living with disabilities, including substance use disorders, mental illness, dual diagnosis, and/or HIV/AIDS, who have been prioritized through the Alameda County Coordinated Entry System. Participants receive a rental subsidy paired with ongoing supportive services, including housing navigation, tenancy sustaining services, home visits, life skills counseling, benefits advocacy, and case management.

Berkeley Respite
: Also funded by the City of Berkeley, the Berkeley Respite Program is a temporary shelter and intensive housing navigation program serving eight households experiencing homelessness across two shelter homes in Berkeley. Respite is not permanent housing; residents work closely with a Case Manager toward permanent housing, income, and independence, with progress reviewed weekly, monthly, and quarterly.

Position Summary

Under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Housing Case Manager carries a blended caseload across two City of Berkeley–funded programs: approximately 11 Shelter Plus Care participants and 8 households in the Berkeley Respite Program. Shelter Plus Care caseload size is approximate and may fluctuate based on referrals, placements, and contract requirements. For Shelter Plus Care participants, the Housing Case Manager provides housing navigation for those not yet placed and tenancy sustaining services for those in permanent housing, conducting regular home visits throughout Berkeley and Alameda County. For Respite residents, permanent housing placement is the primary goal of every stay: the Housing Case Manager drives an active housing search with each household, builds landlord relationships, removes housing barriers, and supports lease-up and move-in, while also overseeing day-to-day operations of the two shelter homes. The position requires the ability to move fluidly between crisis response, housing search, and long-term stabilization work.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Shelter Plus Care (approximately 11 participants)

Maintain a caseload of approximately 11 Shelter Plus Care participants housed throughout Berkeley and Alameda County; caseload size may fluctuate based on referrals, placements, and contract requirements.
Coordinate the participant intake process; conduct initial assessment and eligibility determination for new referrals received through the Coordinated Entry System; create and maintain participant files electronically in a timely manner.
Provide housing navigation for participants who are not yet placed, including housing search, landlord engagement, unit viewings, application support, document readiness, and move-in assistance.
Provide tenancy sustaining services for housed participants, including lease education, rent payment support, addressing lease violations, mediating landlord and neighbor conflicts, and eviction prevention.
Conduct regular home visits to assess housing stability, unit habitability, and service needs.
Develop individualized service and housing stability plans with each participant; monitor services provided and update plans regularly.
Assist participants with Activities of Daily Living (ADL) skills, budgeting and money management, and household upkeep.
Facilitate Medi-Cal applications; engage in referral, coordination, and monitoring of Medi-Cal services; arrange or provide non-emergency, non-medical transportation to Medi-Cal covered services.
Provide benefits advocacy and assist participants in applying for and maintaining income, including SSI, SSDI, General Assistance, and employment.
Work closely with City of Berkeley Shelter Plus Care program staff, subsidy administrators, and property owners.

Berkeley Respite (8 households, two shelter homes)

Provide intensive housing navigation to eight households residing in two Berkeley Respite shelter homes, with permanent housing placement as the primary goal of every resident’s stay.
Conduct resident orientation and intake, including assessment of housing history, barriers, needs, and goals; develop an individualized permanent housing plan with each household early in their stay and update it regularly.
Complete and maintain Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments; monitor CES prioritization lists, advocate for timely permanent housing matches, and attend regional CES case conferences and matching meetings.
Conduct active housing search with residents, including identifying available units, reviewing listings, scheduling and accompanying residents on unit viewings, and completing rental applications.
Locate and build relationships with landlords and property managers willing to rent to Respite residents; match landlord criteria with resident needs and advocate on residents’ behalf.
Complete documentation for housing such as identification, income and benefits verification, credit and rental history, and required program documentation so households can obtain housing.
Identify and address housing barriers, including past evictions, poor or limited credit, criminal history, and lack of rental history.
Assist residents in applying for and maintaining income, including SSI, SSDI, General Assistance, CalFresh, and employment; connect residents to benefits advocacy and employment services.
Work with residents to build budgets and save toward move-in costs; identify and secure deposits, move-in assistance, and household goods, including arranging off-site storage as residents prepare to move.
Meet with residents regularly, both one-on-one and in group house meetings, to review housing plan progress weekly, monthly, and quarterly.
Support lease-up and move-in, including lease review, unit walk-through, utility setup, and coordination of transportation and furnishings; provide warm handoffs to permanent supportive housing providers or ongoing case management as applicable.
Follow up with residents after placement to support early housing stability and reduce returns to homelessness.
Oversee day-to-day operations of the two shelter homes in support of residents’ housing goals, including weekly and as-needed room checks to confirm rooms are safe, clean, pest-free, and within belongings guidelines.
Uphold program guidelines; issue verbal and written warnings, develop behavioral contracts, and prepare exit documentation in coordination with the Program Manager.
Maintain the confidentiality of shelter locations and enforce visitor, overnight attendance, smoking, alcohol and drug, and weapons policies.
Respond to maintenance and repair requests and coordinate with contracted vendors and facilities staff; support bed bug prevention and response protocols.
Assist residents with move-out logistics and transportation upon exit from the program.

Both Programs

Provide crisis intervention as needed, including coordination with the Mobile Crisis Unit and emergency services.
Effectively seek out and use community resources; make referrals and linkages to medical and dental care, mental health and substance use treatment, benefits enrollment, legal services, employment services, and domestic violence services.
Maintain accurate records and prepare monthly and quarterly statistical and narrative reports for the City of Berkeley in a timely manner.
Maintain HMIS database records, including participant intake, program entry, and program exit; ensure data is entered within required timeframes.
Adhere to laws regarding confidentiality and reporting requirements; maintain knowledge of HIPAA standards.
Address participant concerns and grievances at the first level and escalate to the Program Manager in accordance with the agency grievance procedure.
Respond to reasonable accommodation requests and coordinate review with the Program Manager.
Work closely with other agency case managers and counselors to ensure consistency in philosophical and practical approaches to services.
Drive own or agency vehicle to various sites as required; document and report mileage according to agency procedures so that services can be provided in a timely manner; comply with agency driving policy at all times.
Participate in promoting a safe, healthy, and clean working environment consistent with the agency’s health and safety practices.
Attend and participate in all meetings and trainings as assigned.
Complete and submit timesheets in a timely and accurate manner.
Work within the framework of Insight Housing’s Code of Conduct.
Perform other tasks as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

High school required. Bachelor’s degree in Social Services or a related field a plus.
One year of experience providing direct support services to individuals experiencing homelessness, mental health conditions, substance use, or other social issues, required. Translatable military experience, relevant internship and volunteer experience, or administrative experience will be considered. Prior customer service, mentorship, administrative, extensive documentation, or experience providing life skills training or eligibility advisement will be considered.
Proficient in use of computer and Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a shelter or congregate residential setting.
Knowledge of HIV/AIDS.

Training or certification in trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, or similar evidence-based practices.
Bilingual or multilingual abilities relevant to the population served.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Commitment to serving individuals experiencing homelessness, alcohol and drug dependency, and other mental health conditions, and to a trauma-informed approach to care.
Ability to balance a blended caseload across two programs with different service models, settings, and documentation requirements.
Ability to set and hold clear, consistent boundaries in a congregate shelter setting while maintaining supportive, respectful relationships with residents.
Ability to interact in a supportive and professional manner with staff and program participants of diverse cultural and economic backgrounds.

Capable of working independently and as part of a team.

Build and maintain strong relationships with service providers, shelter staff, and community organizations to ensure coordinated care.
Assist residents with completing intake forms, understanding shelter expectations, and available resources.
The Case Manager will work in person, one-on-one with each resident to develop personalized housing stability plans. jobs.title: Housing Navigator Albany Project Hope
jobs.description:
Company Overview

For more than 50 years, Insight Housing has provided a comprehensive range of housing, food, and support services to help those in need move from homelessness into a safe and affordable home of their own. We serve in seven counties in the bay area - Alameda, San Francisco, Contra Costa, Solano, Sacramento, San Joaquin, and Amador County. We are proud of our team members who are very dedicated to our mission of ensuring everyone in our community has a home through supportive, equitable, and sustainable housing solutions.

Program Overview

Albany Project Hope
: Since July 2013, Insight Housing has provided street outreach and housing navigation to residents of the City of Albany experiencing homelessness. Outreach is the core of the program: staff conduct daily field-based outreach routes throughout Albany to engage unsheltered residents, complete Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments, and connect people to housing and services. The program also operates one 4-bedroom master-leased transitional home providing shelter for up to four households through December 2026; the home is scheduled to close January 1, 2027, after which the program transitions to full-time street outreach and housing navigation. Services are delivered using Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma-Informed Care, and Progressive Engagement models. Insight Housing serves as a key CES access point for the City of Albany and works in close partnership with Albany CARES, the Albany Police Department, and regional homeless service providers.

Position Summary

Under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Housing Navigator is responsible for street outreach, engagement, housing navigation, and case management for Albany residents experiencing homelessness. This is a field-based position: the majority of the workday is spent outdoors on assigned outreach routes, engaging unsheltered residents where they are rather than working from an office. The Housing Navigator builds trusting relationships through consistent, persistent engagement, completes CES assessments, develops housing stability plans, and supports participants through housing search, placement, and retention. Through January 2027, the Housing Navigator also provides case management to residents of the program’s emergency shelter house and supports their transition to permanent housing prior to the home’s closure.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Conduct daily, field-based street outreach along assigned routes throughout the City of Albany — including the community center, the senior center, the areas around the Safeway and Target stores, Albany Hill, the shower program at the Albany Aquatic Center, Solano and San Pablo Avenues, and the Ohlone Greenway — and other locations where people experiencing homelessness congregate.
Build and sustain trusting relationships with unsheltered residents through consistent, persistent engagement, using Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma-Informed Care, and Progressive Engagement approaches.
Distribute outreach and basic needs supplies, including hygiene items, weather-appropriate clothing, water, and snacks.
Respond to outreach referrals and crisis requests from City of Albany staff, Albany CARES, the Albany Police Department, and community partners.
Assist participants in meeting basic needs for food, shelter, medical and mental health care, identification documents, and benefits enrollment.
Complete Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments for all consenting participants engaged through outreach.
Develop and update individual housing stability plans at least every 90 days for all engaged program participants.
Monitor CES prioritization lists, advocate for timely permanent housing matches, and attend regional CES case conferences and matching meetings.
Provide ongoing housing search and navigation support, including obtaining identification documents, applying for and maintaining income, addressing past evictions or poor credit, and building independent living skills.
Make referrals and linkages to medical care, mental health and substance use treatment, benefits enrollment, legal services, employment services, domestic violence services, and veterans services; coordinate warm handoffs to permanent supportive housing providers upon match.
Administer flexible housing support funds for barrier removal: transportation assistance, document fees, emergency clothing and food, and essential household items, consistent with participant housing stability plans and agency financial procedures.
Provide case management to residents of the program’s 4-bedroom master-leased emergency shelter house, which shelters up to four households and is scheduled to close January 1, 2027; conduct resident intake and enrollment, hold weekly case management meetings, and support life skills development including cleaning, cooking, budgeting, and tenant responsibilities.
Support the responsible wind-down of the transitional home by ensuring all residents secure safe exits to permanent housing through CES matches or other appropriate placements prior to closure; transition to full-time street outreach and housing navigation following closure.
Complete enrollment in HMIS within 24 hours of acceptance of services and enter case notes within 72 hours of each participant interaction.
Maintain and track documentation of outreach contacts for individuals not yet enrolled in services, using the Albany outreach tracking spreadsheet.
Prepare monthly and quarterly statistical and narrative program reports for the City of Albany, and provide accurate participant and outreach data as needed by the Program Manager.
Adhere to laws regarding confidentiality and reporting requirements; maintain HMIS data security protocols and knowledge of HIPAA standards.
Maintain collaborative working relationships with City of Albany staff, Albany CARES, the Albany Police Department, and other service providers; attend City-convened coordination meetings, monthly Albany CARES case conferences, and North County Homeless Resource Center meetings.
Drive own vehicle to outreach sites and other program locations as required; document and report mileage according to agency procedures so that services can be provided in a timely manner; comply with agency driving policy at all times.
Participate in promoting a safe, healthy, and clean working environment consistent with the agency’s health and safety practices.
Attend and participate in all meetings and trainings as assigned.
Complete and submit timesheets in a timely and accurate manner.
Work within the framework of Insight Housing’s Code of Conduct.
Perform other tasks as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

High school required. Bachelor’s degree in Social Services or a related field a plus.
One year of experience providing direct support services to individuals experiencing homelessness, mental health conditions, substance use, or other social issues, required. Translatable military experience, relevant internship and volunteer experience, or administrative experience will be considered. Prior customer service, mentorship, administrative, extensive documentation, or experience providing life skills training or eligibility advisement will be considered.
Willingness and ability to perform field-based work, spending the majority of the workday outdoors and on foot in varying weather conditions.
Proficient in use of computer and Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams).
Ability to complete CPR/First Aid training.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience conducting street outreach and engagement with unsheltered individuals.
Experience with the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) and Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments.
Experience with transitional housing or housing retention programs.
Lived experience of homelessness or housing instability.
Training or certification in trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, or similar evidence-based practices.
Bilingual or multilingual abilities relevant to the population served.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Commitment to serving individuals experiencing homelessness, with understanding of and sensitivity to issues affecting people who are unhoused, low income, or living with mental health conditions or substance use disorders.
Ability to interact in a supportive and professional manner with staff and program participants of diverse cultural and economic backgrounds.
Ability to provide good customer service; communicate effectively and maintain a calm demeanor in stressful situations.
Capable of working independently and as part of a team, with minimal day-to-day supervision in a field-based setting.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Excellent interpersonal and crisis intervention skills with a can-do and flexible attitude; ability to work well under high pressure.
Ability to multitask, manage competing priorities, maintain confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries, and meet deadlines.
Ability to maintain professional conduct, attitude, and appearance at all times.

Special Requirements

This position requires frequent driving. A valid California driver license, reliable personal vehicle, current personal auto insurance as required by law, and an MVR sufficient to obtain and reasonably maintain insurability under agency auto liability policies.
Must be able to receive and maintain criminal records clearance.
Must be able to obtain TB clearance.

Physical Requirements

Regularly required to use hands and fingers to handle, feel, or operate objects, tools or controls, and reach with hands and arms.

Family Tree Private Care is a leading and trusted provider of concierge-level advisory services to older adults, those living with disabilities, and their families. Family Tree Private Care is an ideal fit if you are looking for a fulfilling opportunity, passionate teammates, and a growing company to help support your career.

Despite our growth, we remain most proud of two things: Our premier reputation in the communities we serve and our culture of developing and promoting future leaders from within the company.

Job Summary

The Case Manager will be responsible for managing relationships with clients, serving as a trusted advisor to the families we serve and maximizing customer loyalty. To be successful in this role, one must have an eagerness for delivering exceptional care to clients and be willing to go above and beyond to ensure utmost client satisfaction.

To be a Case Manager, one should have a passion for taking care of older adults and persons with disabilities and have an interest in driving quality health outcomes through ensuring quality caregiving services. Top candidates have worked in a clinical setting or have strong customer service experience and are skilled at leading conversations and building relationships.

Role And Responsibilities

In-Home Visits (Assessments/Follow-Up)
Perform initial in-home assessments in clients’ homes to determine care needs and develop appropriate plans of care for families in need.
Establish a strong first impression when visiting new clients to ensure high rate of conversion from prospect to client.
Maximize sales potential by building a strong rapport with families, developing a thorough understanding of customer needs/requirements, and providing recommendations on the best arrangement of services (caregiving, nursing, and/or care management).
Ensure successful onboarding of new clients (e.g. new client paperwork)
Establish transparency with pricing and cost of services prior to start.
Ongoing Client Support (Issue Management)

As a Population Health Care Manager, RN, you’ll play an important role in helping high-risk and medically complex patients navigate their care across the continuum. The Social Worker
is responsible to act as a liaison and assists in coordinating resources for the care of health plan members with multiple co-morbidities and/or psychosocial needs. The primary scope is to provide counseling and assistance to patients and their families as requested with personal, financial, ethical, and environmental difficulties that predispose patients to illness. The Social Worker acts as an advocate for members and their families linking them to community resources and financial assistance programs for continued growth toward a maximum level of independence. The Social Worker will interact and collaborate with the interdisciplinary care team, which includes physicians, nurses, case managers, pharmacists, laboratory technologists, other social workers, dietitians, and other educators.

The Social Worker (SW)
is responsible and accountable for coordination of patient services through an interdisciplinary process, which provides clinical and psychosocial approach through continuum of care. Discharge planning will begin at the time of (or prior to) admission, and reassessed ongoing throughout the course of hospitalization. Provides direct social work/case management services to patients and/or families and hospital staff to ensure needed assessment intervention, support, and referral. Coordinates services with other members of the health care team community wide. Respond to information and referral needs of the community. The foundation of the SW role includes crisis intervention, comprehensive understanding of mental health diagnosis, brief counseling, working collaboratively with community vendors, identifying resource needs, arrange and facilitate meetings with the health care team as needed, problem solving and promoting patient wellness.

Involves staff at the next level of care when appropriate to promote continuity of care
Interfaces with Department Leaders, Risk Management and patient representatives to identify potential QA or risk issues

2+ years of experience working in a healthcare setting

Oral & written communication skills

Basic Requirements

United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy
Education: Master's degree in social work (MSW) from a school of social work fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE)

A doctoral degree in social work may not be substituted for master's degree in social work

Grade Determinations: One year of experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level
Experience must demonstrate possession of advanced practice skills and judgment - demonstrating progressively more professional competency
Candidate may have certification or other post-master's degree training from a nationally recognized professional organization or university that includes a defined curriculum/course of study and internship - or equivalent supervised professional experience
Demonstrated Knowledge - Skills - and Abilities
In addition to the experience above - the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: (a) Knowledge of program coordination and administration which includes consultation - negotiation - and monitoring
(b) Knowledge and ability to write policies - procedures - and/or practice guidelines for the program
(c) Ability to supervise multidisciplinary staff assigned to the program
(d) Skill in organizing work - setting priorities - meeting multiple deadlines - and evaluating assigned program area(s)
(e) Ability to provide training - orientation - and guidance within clinical practice
Preferred Experience: Clinical experience conducting assessments and coordinating complex care
Working with individuals experiencing homelessness

Outreach to and development of partnerships with community partners including landlords - group homes - and other partners able to assist Veterans with long-term housing Assisting with program improvement projects - and program development to meet Directives and other guidance specific to the HCHV and HUD-VASH Programs
Clinical consultation and guidance for GS9/11 Social Workers in HUD-VASH
Providing ongoing education and training for GS9/11 Social Workers specific to case management practices and expectations - and treatment planning

Responds to Consults and Homeless Hotline calls by conducting assessments and connecting Veterans to appropriate services
Conducts outreach - attending community events - and seeking to identify Veterans who may benefit from HCHV and HUD-VASH support services
Verifies the veteran's status - eligibility for VA medical care - and eligibility of program participation
Assisting Veterans with completion of paperwork and processes related to securing housing and/or other supportive services

Responsibilities

Job Summary

In alignment with Brookdale’s Resident and Family Engagement philosophy, plans, coordinates and facilitates a calendar of person centered dementia friendly programs that meet specific needs of each and all residents within the dementia care community. Provides person centered programs while engaging residents in meaningful and purposeful dementia care programs within the Brookdale community enhancing their quality of life. Recognizes individual abilities and needs while encouraging independence and ensuring resident habits, historical routines, interests and preferences are honored in the provision of care and programming.

Essential Functions

Designs a 7 day a week person centered program that is engaging, creative and meets the needs and interests of the individual residents. Promotes and engages residents in the 7 domains of well-being programs in a dementia friendly structured environment; including sensory focused small group programming for residents who cannot participate in a larger group setting.
Develops a monthly calendar, in partnership with residents, based on residents’ shared interests. Ensures person centered special events and daily path programs are scheduled and executed as scheduled.
Ensures dementia care programs are in compliance with Brookdale Excellence Standards Tool (BEST), Divisional Dementia Care Site visit tool, state, federal, and other regulations and meet Brookdale’s mission, policies, procedures and dementia care standards as assigned by the Executive Director.
Collaborates with community leadership educating & providing resources to families and associates regarding Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias. This includes how to engage residents and lead programs on an ongoing basis. This includes facilitating and coordinating dementia focused in-services and or events for families or computer based and situation specific training for associates including Understanding Alzheimer’s & Dementia Care (UADC), as required by Brookdale.
May provide direct supervision of Clare Bridge Program Assistant/s, as required by Executive Director, which includes assisting with hiring, coaching, and counseling program assistant associate and conducting the documenting corrective action, as needed. Collaborates with community leadership in planning, coordinating, appropriately decorating, and participating in special events including holidays, signature programs, National Walk to End Alzheimer’s, family socials, educational and marketing events.
Reports changes in residents’ overall health to clinical partner, including changes in behavior; takes actions to address concerns in a timely manner and collaborates with the team in exploring approaches and interventions to address behavioral expressions.

Performs personal care, housekeeping and dietary responsibilities, as needed, to ensure service quality is maintained in accordance with Clare Bridge Program standards. Has completed training and qualifications based on state regulations to ensure service quality is maintained in accordance with Clare Bridge Program standards.

jobs.title: Sustainability Program Specialist
jobs.description:
The Sustainability Program Specialists are key contributors to the continued growth and success of IAS sustainability programs and initiatives that help growers capture value through stewardship, carbon-intensity improvement, nutrient management, conservation, and market opportunities.

Sustainability Program Specialist

Location: East Central Iowa (Monticello, Masonville or similar area)

About Sustainability Programs At Innovative Ag Services

At Innovative Ag Services (IAS), we believe sustainability should create measurable value for our farmer members. Through our sustainability programs and partnerships, we help growers pursue opportunities related to conservation, nutrient stewardship, carbon intensity improvement, low-carbon grain markets, and emerging sustainability incentives.

IAS sustainability efforts connect agronomic expertise, farm data, stewardship practices, conservation resources, and market opportunities to help growers improve profitability while enhancing the long-term productivity of their operations. As programs, partnerships, and market requirements continue to evolve, IAS is committed to providing practical solutions that help farmers succeed.

Who We Are Looking For

IAS is seeking a highly motivated, organized, and relationship-focused individual to support the growth and delivery of IAS sustainability programs and initiatives. This specialist will work directly with growers, Agronomy Sales Advisors, grain personnel, and industry partners to support opportunities that create value for both farmers and IAS.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working with farm data, sustainability programs, carbon intensity metrics, nutrient management concepts, and grower-facing communications. They are passionate about agriculture, committed to helping farmers succeed, and capable of navigating a rapidly evolving sustainability landscape.

Position Summary

The Sustainability Program Specialist is responsible for supporting the administration, implementation, and growth of IAS sustainability programs and related initiatives. This position serves as a key resource for growers and internal teams by coordinating program enrollment, collecting and managing agricultural data, supporting carbon intensity and nutrient stewardship initiatives, assisting with conservation practice implementation, and helping growers participate in sustainability opportunities.

This role combines agronomy, project management, sustainability, data analysis, and customer service to help farmers maximize the value of their stewardship efforts while preparing for market and regulatory opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Sustainability Program Administration

Serve as a primary point of contact for growers participating in IAS sustainability programs and initiatives.
Support grower enrollment and onboarding into sustainability programs.
Manage program records and maintain accurate grower documentation.
Coordinate grower communications regarding program requirements, opportunities, deadlines, and reporting.
Track participation metrics and support continuous improvement of IAS sustainability program offerings.
Work closely with sustainability leadership to expand program enrollment and grower engagement.

Sustainability Data, Measurement & Reporting

Assist with the collection, validation, and management of farm management data used in carbon intensity calculations.
Support development and distribution of grower sustainability and carbon intensity reports.
Help growers understand the agronomic and management factors influencing carbon intensity scores.
Assist in identifying opportunities for growers to improve environmental performance and capture additional program value.
Support documentation requirements associated with low-carbon grain, biofuel, and sustainability programs.

Nutrient Stewardship & Program Readiness

Support development and documentation of nutrient management plans and nutrient budgets.
Assist growers in implementing 4R Nutrient Stewardship practices.
Work with Agronomy Sales Advisors to develop sound agronomic recommendations.
Help maintain documentation required for sustainability, regulatory, and market-based programs.
Stay informed on evolving sustainability policies, biofuel regulations, and program requirements impacting growers.

Conservation & Soil Health Programs

Educate growers on conservation and soil health practices, including reduced tillage, cover crops, nutrient management, and water quality initiatives.
Assist growers with participation in conservation incentive and cost-share programs.
Coordinate with conservation agencies, watershed groups, and industry partners to support project implementation.
Promote adoption of practices that improve soil health, nutrient efficiency, and long-term farm sustainability.

Data Management & Analysis

Utilize sustainability software platforms and agricultural data systems to manage grower information.
Review field-level management records for completeness, accuracy, and program eligibility.
Analyze sustainability performance metrics and prepare grower-facing reports.
Support internal reporting and project tracking requirements.
Maintain confidential grower records and ensure data integrity.

Grower & Employee Education

Serve as an educational resource for IAS employees and customers regarding sustainability programs and opportunities.
Assist in creating grower communications, presentations, training materials, and educational resources.
Support sustainability training initiatives for Agronomy Sales Advisors and other internal stakeholders.
Represent IAS at grower meetings, field days, industry events, and educational programs.

Required Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Soil Science, Agricultural Business, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, or related field.
Minimum of three years of experience in agriculture, agronomy, conservation, sustainability, or project management.
Understanding of Midwestern crop production systems and farm management practices.
Experience working directly with growers and agricultural stakeholders.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data management systems.
Excellent communication, organization, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of sustainability measurement, environmental outcomes reporting, carbon intensity concepts, and agricultural market or incentive programs.
Understanding nutrient management planning and 4R Nutrient Stewardship principles.
Experience working with USDA, NRCS, IDALS, SWCD, or other conservation initiatives.

Competencies & Skills

Strong project management and organizational skills.
Exceptional attention to detail and data accuracy.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Customer-focused mindset with a passion for serving growers.
Ability to communicate technical information in a practical and understandable manner.
Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

Physical Requirements / Environmental Adaptability

Ability to travel throughout the IAS trade territory to visit farms, attend meetings, and support field activities.
Ability to work in both office and agricultural field environments.
Occasional exposure to outdoor weather conditions and agricultural production settings.
Ability to lift, push, pull, or carry up to 50 pounds.
May require use of personal protective equipment when appropriate.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working with farm data, sustainability programs, carbon intensity metrics, nutrient management concepts, and grower-facing communications. They are passionate about agriculture, committed to helping farmers succeed, and capable of navigating a rapidly evolving sustainability landscape.

Position Summary

The Sustainability Program Specialist is responsible for supporting the administration, implementation, and growth of IAS sustainability programs and related initiatives. This position serves as a key resource for growers and internal teams by coordinating program enrollment, collecting and managing agricultural data, supporting carbon intensity and nutrient stewardship initiatives, assisting with conservation practice implementation, and helping growers participate in sustainability opportunities.

This role combines agronomy, project management, sustainability, data analysis, and customer service to help farmers maximize the value of their stewardship efforts while preparing for market and regulatory opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Sustainability Program Administration

Serve as a primary point of contact for growers participating in IAS sustainability programs and initiatives.
Support grower enrollment and onboarding into sustainability programs.
Manage program records and maintain accurate grower documentation.
Coordinate grower communications regarding program requirements, opportunities, deadlines, and reporting.
Track participation metrics and support continuous improvement of IAS sustainability program offerings.
Work closely with sustainability leadership to expand program enrollment and grower engagement.

Sustainability Data, Measurement & Reporting

Assist with the collection, validation, and management of farm management data used in carbon intensity calculations.
Support development and distribution of grower sustainability and carbon intensity reports.
Help growers understand the agronomic and management factors influencing carbon intensity scores.
Assist in identifying opportunities for growers to improve environmental performance and capture additional program value.
Support documentation requirements associated with low-carbon grain, biofuel, and sustainability programs.

Nutrient Stewardship & Program Readiness

Support development and documentation of nutrient management plans and nutrient budgets.
Assist growers in implementing 4R Nutrient Stewardship practices.
Work with Agronomy Sales Advisors to develop sound agronomic recommendations.
Help maintain documentation required for sustainability, regulatory, and market-based programs.
Stay informed on evolving sustainability policies, biofuel regulations, and program requirements impacting growers.

Conservation & Soil Health Programs

Educate growers on conservation and soil health practices, including reduced tillage, cover crops, nutrient management, and water quality initiatives.
Assist growers with participation in conservation incentive and cost-share programs.
Coordinate with conservation agencies, watershed groups, and industry partners to support project implementation.
Promote adoption of practices that improve soil health, nutrient efficiency, and long-term farm sustainability.

Data Management & Analysis

Utilize sustainability software platforms and agricultural data systems to manage grower information.
Review field-level management records for completeness, accuracy, and program eligibility.
Analyze sustainability performance metrics and prepare grower-facing reports.
Support internal reporting and project tracking requirements.
Maintain confidential grower records and ensure data integrity.

Grower & Employee Education

Serve as an educational resource for IAS employees and customers regarding sustainability programs and opportunities.
Assist in creating grower communications, presentations, training materials, and educational resources.
Support sustainability training initiatives for Agronomy Sales Advisors and other internal stakeholders.
Represent IAS at grower meetings, field days, industry events, and educational programs.

Required Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Soil Science, Agricultural Business, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, or related field.
Minimum of three years of experience in agriculture, agronomy, conservation, sustainability, or project management.
Understanding of Midwestern crop production systems and farm management practices.
Experience working directly with growers and agricultural stakeholders.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data management systems.
Excellent communication, organization, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of sustainability measurement, environmental outcomes reporting, carbon intensity concepts, and agricultural market or incentive programs.
Understanding nutrient management planning and 4R Nutrient Stewardship principles.
Experience working with USDA, NRCS, IDALS, SWCD, or other conservation initiatives.

Competencies & Skills

Strong project management and organizational skills.
Exceptional attention to detail and data accuracy.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Customer-focused mindset with a passion for serving growers.
Ability to communicate technical information in a practical and understandable manner.
Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

Physical Requirements / Environmental Adaptability

Ability to travel throughout the IAS trade territory to visit farms, attend meetings, and support field activities.
Ability to work in both office and agricultural field environments.
Occasional exposure to outdoor weather conditions and agricultural production settings.
Ability to lift, push, pull, or carry up to 50 pounds.
May require use of personal protective equipment when appropriate.

jobs.description:
Posting Number:
SP005464P

Division/College:
College of Education, Health & Human Sciences

Department:
